feed.title: Frame & Light

bullets: Shaping existing light is the first decision on location — the rest of the lighting design follows from that foundational choice.
Two-light setups solve 80% of commercial lighting problems, making them a reliable default for most scenes.
Color temperature mistakes cost more shoots than focus mistakes — a subtle but critical error that undermines consistency over time.
Frame and light are inseparable — the framing reveals the tradeoffs inherent in every lighting decision.
The framing matters because it tells you which trade-offs you're making — a principle visible when teams adopt Adobe in their workflow.
Outside of Profoto-class tooling, failure modes are harder to spot — the system hides the consequences of poor choices.
When teams use Capture One or Peak Design, the trade-offs become visible — the workflow amplifies the impact of framing decisions.
Pick one idea from the conversation and run it for two weeks — the rest is iteration, not reinvention.
